method:rack::engine::Module::onExpanderC.finding: P2: the other eleven events have a direct raw call, but onExpanderChange does not. native/bindings/engine/module.cpp:764-776 binds on_add through on_unset_master only, so there is no rackpy.raw.engine.Module.on_expander_change(e). Outside the laboratory, C++'s direct call Module::onExpanderChange(e) on an ordinary module (Rack's empty behaviour plus RackPy's snapshot) has no raw mapping. method_template:rack::engine::Module::co.finding: P2: config_button accepts only a SwitchQuantity subclass as quantity_type (native/bindings/engine/module.cpp:1017 passes switchOnly=true; native/bindings/engine/standalone_quantity.cpp:215). Rack's configButton<TSwitchQuantity> touches only ParamQuantity members (Module.hpp:164-171), so configButton<SomeParamQuantity> is valid C++. config_switch legitimately needs SwitchQuantity because it sets SwitchQuantity::labels. Smallest fix: let config_button accept any ParamQuantity subclass, or document the narrowing.

P1: unjustified restriction. config_param rejects non-finite (unbounded) bounds, min >= max, a default outside [min, max] and display_base of 1 or -1 (native/module/module.hpp:482-485). Rack's configParam accepts all of these and only asserts the ID (Module.hpp:124-147). Rack supports unbounded quantities (Quantity::isBounded), and RP-14's own contract (planning/rp-14-slices.md:152) says to preserve raw unbounded and equal bounds. The cited docs admit the helper 'does not cover arbitrary unbounded/raw C++ configuration semantics' (docs/reference/engine-module.md:314-317). No owner approval is recorded, and none of these cases crashes Rack or is undefined behaviour. Smallest fix: accept Rack's full argument range and keep only the ID check, or record an owner-approved contract for the restriction.

P1: unjustified restriction. config_switch runs through the same validation (native/bindings/engine/module.cpp:1004-1008, then native/module/module.hpp:482-485), so it rejects equal bounds, non-finite bounds and a default outside the range. Rack's configSwitch accepts these (Module.hpp:152-159). For example, a single-position configSwitch(id, 0, 0, 0, name, {"Only"}) is valid in Rack but refused here. No owner approval is recorded. Smallest fix: same as configParam.
